title: JUKI LBH-1790A-S
subtitle: Computer-Controlled High-Speed Lockstitch Buttonholing Machine
overviewDescription: The JUKI LBH-1790A-S is a computerized lockstitch buttonholing machine. It forms buttonholes by combining mechanical stitch formation with electronic control of feed, needle rocking, tension, knife cutting, trimming, and presser movement.

classificationTable.value: Straight buttonhole sewing for shirts, blouses, uniforms, ladies' wear, and similar garments

workingPrinciples.heading: 1. Pattern Selection and Setup
workingPrinciples.description: The operator selects the buttonhole pattern and settings from the operation panel. The garment is placed under the presser/work clamp. The presser holds the fabric firmly. The control system checks machine safety and sensor conditions.

workingPrinciples.heading: 2. Stitch Formation
workingPrinciples.description: The main motor drives the needle and hook to form lockstitches. The stitch is formed by the upper thread and bobbin thread. The needle carries the upper thread through the fabric, and the full-rotary hook catches the loop to form a lockstitch.

workingPrinciples.heading: 3. Buttonhole Shape Control
workingPrinciples.description: The feed motor controls fabric movement. The needle rocking motor controls side movement of the needle. The buttonhole shape is not controlled by manual movement; it is controlled by the machine's electronic system using motors and stored sewing data.

workingPrinciples.heading: 4. Tension and Cutting
workingPrinciples.description: The active tension system controls thread tension during different sewing sections. The cloth cutting motor drives the knife and cuts the buttonhole slit. The upper and lower trimmers cut the threads. The machine stops and the presser lifts.

workingPrinciples.heading: 5. Quality Factors
workingPrinciples.description: The final buttonhole quality depends on needle condition, hook timing, thread tension, fabric holding, knife setting, sensor accuracy, and stable electronic control.

sequenceFlow.stepDescription: Garment placed under presser / work clamp
Control system checks sensors and safety
Feed and needle rocking motors form buttonhole shape; active tension controls thread tension
Cloth cutting motor drives knife; upper and lower trimmers cut threads
Good piece goes to next operation; defective piece goes for rework or mechanic check

finalNotes:
• Needle: Replace immediately when damaged or unstable stitching appears. Use DP×5, #11J to #14J.
• Hook Timing: Check and adjust hook timing if skipped stitches or thread breakage occurs.
• Knife: Sharpen or replace when buttonhole slit is not clean.
• Boards: Replace MAIN/SDC/FLT/INT PCB only after checking voltage, grounding, fan, motor, connector, and sensor condition.
• Sensors: Clean and adjust origin sensors before replacing.
• Fuses: Always find the root cause before replacing fuses.
• Fan Motor: Replace weak or non-rotating fan motor to protect control boards from heat damage.
